tagline: Andrew Ng's governed AI coworker, run on local models with no cloud key

scenes.narration: Day 49: OpenWorker, Andrew Ng's AI coworker, run headless on a local model with no cloud API key.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: An agent that reads, writes and runs tools in your files
Every tool call is approval-gated by default
Every call is logged, approved or denied
scenes.narration: OpenWorker is a coworker agent that works in your files and tools. By design, every tool call needs approval, and every call gets logged either way.

steps.narration: We ran the CLI headless, isolated from any real settings, pointed at a local llama.cpp server serving Qwen2.5, no cloud key involved.
When the model calls a tool like write_file, the approval gate decides: in ask mode with no terminal attached, it is refused before it runs.
Either way, approved or denied, the call lands in a SQLite audit log: proposed, resolved, finished.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Qwen2.5-3B's two read_file calls both failed on a wrong path, yet brief.md still got written.
scenes.narration: In ask mode, a write_file call was denied and logged, with brief.md never created. With approvals bypassed, the call ran, but a 3B model's two read_file calls both hit a wrong path, and it wrote a placeholder brief without ever reading the real notes.
The approval gate worked exactly as documented. Whether the model behind it could be trusted with the task was a separate question.
